\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{झडती} \mr{घेणे} (jhaḍtī gheṇe)}{झडती घेणे (jhaḍtī gheṇe)}]{\mr{झडती} \mr{घेणे} (jhaḍtī gheṇe) — to search a place}

\label{lesson:MR-C299-jhadti-ghene}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for a mob, then the Marathi for to whisper.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{झडती} \mr{घेणे}}
\textbf{\mr{झडती} \mr{घेणे}} — \emph{jhaḍtī gheṇe} — \textquotedblleft{}to search a place\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mr{पोलिसांनी} \mr{संशयिताच्या} \mr{घराची} \mr{झडती} \mr{घेतली}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{polisānnī saṁśayitācyā gharācī jhaḍtī ghetlī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police searched the suspect's house.
\end{quote}

Past, with -\mr{ने} (he …): \mr{त्याने} \mr{झडती} \mr{घेतली}, \emph{tyāne jhaḍtī ghetlī}.

What is searched takes -\mr{ची}: \mr{घराची} \mr{झडती} \mr{घेणे}. \mr{झडती} is feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{झडती} \mr{घेणे}} (\emph{jhaḍtī gheṇe}) joins \emph{jhaḍtī}, 'a search', to \emph{gheṇe}, 'to take'; the origin of \emph{jhaḍtī} is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jhaḍtī gheṇe}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jhaḍtī gheṇe}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{polisānnī saṁśayitācyā gharācī jhaḍtī ghetlī.} — The police searched the suspect's house.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marathi for a mob, then the Marathi for to whisper, then say \emph{jhaḍtī gheṇe} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \mr{झडती} \mr{घेणे} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To search a place\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{पंचनामा} (pañcnāmā)}{पंचनामा (pañcnāmā)}]{\mr{पंचनामा} (pañcnāmā) — a scene report; an official record of a scene}

\label{lesson:MR-C299-pancnama}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for to whisper, then the Marathi for to search a place.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{पंचनामा}}
\textbf{\mr{पंचनामा}} — \emph{pañcnāmā} — \textquotedblleft{}a scene report; an official record of a scene\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mr{हवालदाराने} \mr{घटनास्थळी} \mr{पंचनामा} \mr{केला}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{havāldārāne ghaṭnāsthaḷī pañcnāmā kelā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The constable drew up an official report at the scene.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\mr{पंचनामा} \mr{करणे}, to draw one up, signed by witnesses.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{पंचनामा}} (\emph{pañcnāmā}) is built from \emph{pañc}, 'five; the panel of witnesses', from Sanskrit \emph{pañca} (Monier-Williams), and Persian \emph{nāma}, 'a writing, a document'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pañcnāmā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pañcnāmā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{havāldārāne ghaṭnāsthaḷī pañcnāmā kelā.} — The constable drew up an official report at the scene.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marathi for to whisper, then the Marathi for to search a place, then say \emph{pañcnāmā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{जप्त} \mr{करणे} (japta karṇe)}{जप्त करणे (japta karṇe)}]{\mr{जप्त} \mr{करणे} (japta karṇe) — to confiscate; to seize}

\label{lesson:MR-C299-japta-karne}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for to search a place, then the Marathi for a scene report.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{जप्त} \mr{करणे}}
\textbf{\mr{जप्त} \mr{करणे}} — \emph{japta karṇe} — \textquotedblleft{}to confiscate; to seize\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mr{पोलिसांनी} \mr{चोरीची} \mr{गाडी} \mr{जप्त} \mr{केली}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{polisānnī corīcī gāḍī japta kelī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police seized the stolen car.
\end{quote}

Past, with -\mr{ने} (he …): \mr{त्याने} \mr{जप्त} \mr{केलं}, \emph{tyāne japta kelaṁ}.

What is seized agrees with the past: \mr{गाडी} \mr{जप्त} \mr{केली}, \mr{पैसे} \mr{जप्त} \mr{केले}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{जप्त} \mr{करणे}} (\emph{japta karṇe}) joins \emph{japta}, 'seized', a loan from Persian \emph{zabt}, usually traced to Arabic \emph{ḍabṭ}, 'a seizing', to \emph{karṇe}, 'to do'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{कबूल} \mr{करणे} (kabūl karṇe)}{कबूल करणे (kabūl karṇe)}]{\mr{कबूल} \mr{करणे} (kabūl karṇe) — to confess; to admit}

\label{lesson:MR-C299-kabul-karne}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for a scene report, then the Marathi for to confiscate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{कबूल} \mr{करणे}}
\textbf{\mr{कबूल} \mr{करणे}} — \emph{kabūl karṇe} — \textquotedblleft{}to confess; to admit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mr{चौकशीत} \mr{त्याने} \mr{चोरी} \mr{कबूल} \mr{केली}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{caukśīt tyāne corī kabūl kelī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
During questioning he confessed to the theft.
\end{quote}

Past, with -\mr{ने} (he …): \mr{त्याने} \mr{कबूल} \mr{केलं}, \emph{tyāne kabūl kelaṁ}.

What is admitted agrees: \mr{गुन्हा} \mr{कबूल} \mr{केला}, \mr{चूक} \mr{कबूल} \mr{केली}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{कबूल} \mr{करणे}} (\emph{kabūl karṇe}) joins \emph{kabūl}, 'accepted, admitted', a loan from Persian \emph{qabūl}, usually traced to Arabic \emph{qabūl}, 'acceptance', to \emph{karṇe}, 'to do'.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{दाखल} \mr{करणे} (dākhal karṇe)}{दाखल करणे (dākhal karṇe)}]{\mr{दाखल} \mr{करणे} (dākhal karṇe) — to file; to admit}

\label{lesson:MR-C299-dakhal-karne}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for to confiscate, then the Marathi for to confess.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{दाखल} \mr{करणे}}
\textbf{\mr{दाखल} \mr{करणे}} — \emph{dākhal karṇe} — \textquotedblleft{}to file; to admit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mr{तिने} \mr{पोलीस} \mr{ठाण्यात} \mr{तक्रार} \mr{दाखल} \mr{केली}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tine polīs ṭhāṇyāt takrār dākhal kelī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She filed a complaint at the police station.
\end{quote}

Past, with -\mr{ने} (he …): \mr{त्याने} \mr{दाखल} \mr{केलं}, \emph{tyāne dākhal kelaṁ}.

\mr{रुग्णालयात} \mr{दाखल} \mr{करणे}, to admit to hospital; \mr{गुन्हा} \mr{दाखल} \mr{करणे}, to register a case.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{दाखल} \mr{करणे}} (\emph{dākhal karṇe}) joins \emph{dākhal}, 'entered, admitted', a loan from Persian \emph{dāxil}, usually traced to Arabic \emph{dākhil}, 'entering', to \emph{karṇe}, 'to do'.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for telling what happened.
